expected.summary: After forward annotation, with the 70 x 48 mm outline: places J1, C1, R1 and D1 by their connections in the DEMO group and writes the zone label; each part reads back placed; the board is not saved.
Every component is placed already and --all is not given: nothing to place, the preview lists no change.
--all is a switch and takes no value.
The session has no such board open.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.

Every part is placed, and the outline was made too small for them first (pcb update --width 12mm --height 10mm): the plan puts parts outside the outline, the preview cannot apply, and the runtime refuses it as E_CONFLICT blocked.
Run under a scope file that does not cover the target (the board's components); nothing is previewed to the application's files or sent.

While a forward-annotation run or pcb export job of this tool runs in Layout, the session reports busy or unresponsive. Only --session is given: Layout does not say which board it has open while it does not answer, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Layout before the call, such as Setup > Setup Parameters or Help > About. Layout stops answering COM, the session is reported blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a blocked Layout does not say which board it has open.
Layout goes away while parts are being placed; the components stay locked until operation resolve.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Layout cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: The board holds the forward annotation unsaved, the usual state before the first placement: the parts are placed as usual; the receipt reports the document dirty.

Every part is placed (so the preview plans each position), and the person sets a coarse part grid with snapping in Layout first (Editor Control > Grids, part grid 1 mm): Layout stores each origin on that grid, so x_mm or y_mm reads back more than 0.001 mm from the planned position.
